issues.title: The end-of-turn pause was waited through with nothing in hand
issues.found_on: bench and first calls, median 1210 ms
issues.symptom: Answers began only after the turn closed; about half the turns of the first calls were over 1200 ms.
issues.cause: The recognizer's partial results trail the audio by 300 ms and more, so the words in hand during the pause were short of the sentence and any guess made on them was thrown away at the final.
issues.fix: End the recognition 120 ms into a pause, begin the answer on that final, and open a continuation to hear anything that follows (duplex.early_final_ms).
issues.verified: Bench median 1159 → 943 ms; the pause length no longer adds latency.

issues.title: A guess was made on trailing words while the final was on its way
issues.found_on: box log after 42b5f54
issues.symptom: A prepared answer was thrown away 50–80 ms after it was started.
issues.cause: Speculation on partials still ran in the window between asking for the early final and receiving it.
issues.fix: No guess on partials while an early final is pending.

issues.title: The full stop on an early final was read as 'the caller has finished'
issues.found_on: 13:09 call
issues.symptom: "就是。", "呃。" and "我想问你一下啊。" were taken as finished turns and answered.
issues.cause: A final asked for in a pause ends in "。" whatever was said; it was read as the recognizer's opinion.
issues.fix: The forced stop is ignored when judging whether the caller is done.

issues.title: An interruption was weighed on words that arrived late
issues.found_on: 13:09 call, slowest turn
issues.symptom: Three syllables said over the assistant took 1382 ms to be acted on.
issues.cause: The early final was skipped while a floor hold was undecided, so the decision waited for trailing partials.
issues.fix: The early final is also asked for during an interruption.

issues.title: The latency console refused every golive event
issues.found_on: owner's console showed no golive turns
issues.symptom: None of golive's turns appeared in the console.
issues.cause: The console rejects a whole batch for one unknown key in `extra`; golive sent `agent` on every event.
issues.fix: Only the keys the console accepts are sent.

issues.title: The gateway's turn detection was read as absent
issues.found_on: reading the session.update the gateway sends
issues.symptom: golive believed the gateway sent no end-of-turn setting.
issues.cause: Active Call sends it in camelCase (`silenceDurationMs: 150`).
issues.fix: Both spellings are read; the telephony profile declines 150 ms and keeps 380 (honor_turn_detection: false).
issues.verified: Logged shape of session.update on every call.

issues.title: The first completion of a call was slow
issues.found_on: 14:22 call, first turn 1561 ms
issues.symptom: The first answer of a call took over a second to its first token even with the prompt cached.
issues.cause: The vendor's first completion on a connection and prefix is slow regardless of cache.
issues.fix: A one-token request with the session's instructions while the phone rings and again as the greeting starts (backend_prefix_warm_start).

issues.title: A bare hesitation was answered
issues.found_on: 14:22 call
issues.symptom: "呃" was waited on for 700 ms as a mid-thought and then answered anyway.
issues.cause: Hesitation sounds were treated as words.
issues.fix: Hesitation-only turns are left with the caller (ignore_hesitations).

issues.title: A mid-thought wait cost a whole backend round on top of itself
issues.found_on: 18:34 call, 1481 ms turn
issues.symptom: Words that read as unfinished got 700 ms of patience, and the answer was begun only after it: 700 + ~780 ms.
issues.cause: Speculation was not started while the engine was being patient.
issues.fix: The answer is prepared on the early final during the wait (speculate_while_patient).
issues.verified: Patient turns on later calls: 566–879 ms.

issues.title: A deadline flushed a single character to the synthesizer
issues.found_on: 18:34 call (a regression of dcf68a8)
issues.symptom: The caller heard "加", then "上了吗？".
issues.cause: The shortened first-clause deadline flushed whatever the model had produced, even one character.
issues.fix: The deadline flush waits for stream_first_chunk_chars.
issues.verified: Regression introduced by this work and caught only on a live call.

issues.title: Event ids were reissued after a restart, then made invalid
issues.found_on: 20:18 call: all 70 turns' events refused (a regression)
issues.symptom: The console refused events as duplicates after each restart; the first fix made every id invalid.
issues.cause: Ids were boot id + producer + a count from one; starting the count from the clock made them too long for the console.
issues.fix: Ids carry a short per-run token: boot:<id>:golive-<component>-r<run>:<count>. Probe a new id shape against the console before deploying it.

issues.title: The settled-words close fired 5 ms before the final arrived
issues.found_on: 20:18 call, one of five slow turns
issues.symptom: A turn was closed on stale hypotheses with half the sentence missing.
issues.cause: "No new words for 600 ms" was judged on partials while an early final was pending.
issues.fix: The settled close waits for a final that is on its way.

issues.title: A trailing "啊" threw the prepared answer away
issues.found_on: 20:18 call, one of five slow turns
issues.symptom: The answer begun on "也可以是吧" was discarded when the final read "也可以是吧，啊".
issues.cause: Guess and final were compared exactly.
issues.fix: A trailing interjection is not a different turn (sameWords).

issues.title: Copies of a completion were slow together
issues.found_on: hedge 2 → 4 bought little
issues.symptom: Four copies left one turn in ten slow where independence predicted one in a hundred.
issues.cause: All copies were streams on one HTTP/2 connection on one account.
issues.fix: Each copy goes down a lane: one key on one connection of its own; a pool of keys.
issues.verified: Two accounts: fastest-copy first token p90 504 → 416 ms in 40 rounds. Vendor-wide slow moments remain.

issues.title: Racing every first synthesis hit the vendor's rate limit
issues.found_on: bench on 779002e: 2 of 30 turns lost
issues.symptom: Two answers were never heard: "rate limit exceeded(RPM)".
issues.cause: A second request per turn took the account past its allowance.
issues.fix: Asking both connections every time is off; the second is asked only when the first is slow (tts_hedge_after_ms).
issues.verified: No refusal on any call since.

issues.title: Turns of two or three characters got no head start
issues.found_on: 21:51 and 22:21 calls: all 12 turns without a prepared answer
issues.symptom: Answers to "嗯。" were begun from nothing when the pause ran out; 4 of the 22:21 call's 5 slow turns.
issues.cause: speculative_min_chars, meant for fragments of a hypothesis, was applied to a final asked for in a pause.
issues.fix: The length floor no longer applies to an early final.

issues.title: The synthesizer stalls for seconds on every connection at once
issues.symptom: First audio of 1.3–4 s, and a segment missing for 3.3 s in the middle of an answer. The worst turn so far: 4603 ms.
issues.cause: Not known. Not load: slow syntheses came at 13–17 requests a minute. Not one connection: a second connection asked 260 ms in had nothing either. A probe with TLS handshakes every second caught no stall.
issues.fix: None yet. A second connection (insurance against one bad connection) is in place. Options: the vendor's HTTP endpoint as a second route; a holding phrase on slow turns; openers from the phrase cache. A pool of two accounts is on since 10-12 22:35: an answer's first segment is asked of both and the faster is played. In 30 probe rounds the accounts were never slow together (worst 689 ms alone, 337 for the faster), but no multi-second stall occurred in them, so whether a stall is one account's or everyone's is still not known.

issues.title: The chat model has minutes when every copy is slow
issues.found_on: 21:51 call, 1354 ms turn
issues.symptom: One turn's first token took 845 ms with four copies on two accounts. On 10-12 at 23:14 a whole call sat in one: 12 of 13 turns over 1200 (p50 1309), every one with the first token 577 to 631 ms after the headers; measured outside golive straight after, the fastest of eight copies was at 707 and 712 ms at the median, with every copy over 550 ms in 23 of 24 rounds. The night before, 602 ms at 23:53 and 161 to 202 from 00:08. The same build at 14:28 the next day: 6 turns, p50 831, none over, first token 123 ms after the headers; outside golive 213 and 192 ms. At 21:15 on 10-13, an ordinary evening: 47 turns, p50 884, p95 1045, none over, first token 260 ms after the headers. 10-14 at 15:40, in the afternoon: fastest of eight copies 806 ms at the median, 9 rounds of 10 slow on every copy; one turn of the 15:37 call over 1200 for it.
issues.cause: The vendor as a whole is slow at that moment; and several times slower in its busy hours (602 ms at 23:53 against ~170 ms after midnight).
issues.fix: Eight copies help the ordinary tail (p90 −30 to −100 ms). A second, independent vendor in the race is what would cover these moments.

issues.title: Opening clauses were synthesized again every time
issues.found_on: two calls: 1 answer in 8 opened with words already said
issues.symptom: "好的，", "是的，" and the like waited ~190 ms for the synthesizer on every use.
issues.cause: Only fixed phrases were kept in the phrase cache.
issues.fix: Any answer segment of 12 characters or fewer is remembered and played from memory (phrase_cache_learn_chars). Lost on restart.
issues.verified: 23:08 call: 4 ordinary turns opened from memory, 515–756 ms.

issues.title: The owner's prompt could only be dialled from one browser
issues.found_on: owner asked for a way to call away from the Mac
issues.symptom: A call placed from anywhere but the originator's page ran without the owner's prompt.
issues.cause: The prompt lives in that page's browser storage.
issues.fix: golive keeps the last answered call's instructions and opening line; `phone-brain.sh call` redials them.

issues.title: The request budget starved the hedge it was there to ration
issues.found_on: 09:34 call: both turns over 1200 ms
issues.symptom: The second synthesis connection was refused all four times it was wanted; first audio 938 and 646 ms went unhedged.
issues.cause: The budget capped the account's total at 18 requests a minute; the call made 22.5 a minute by itself.
issues.fix: The budget bounds what hedging adds (4 second requests a minute), not the total.
issues.effect: A second request was wanted twice and allowed twice; none refused. On the call before, four were wanted and four refused.

issues.title: The first-sound echo estimate cannot measure this line
issues.found_on: 09:24 and 09:34 calls
issues.symptom: No measurement on one call; 4 readings against 49 failed attempts on the next, of which two are plausible. On the first recorded call (quiet place) it took 3 readings (300, 620, 740 ms) against 14 failed attempts, and the recording holds no echo to support them.
issues.cause: The idle line is never quiet enough (the caller was on a metro), and the line returns the assistant's voice only some of the time.
issues.fix: Each failed attempt now says why. Replaced by recording the call and correlating over the whole of it (echoprobe).
issues.verified: echoprobe has run on synthetic calls only.

issues.title: The phone leg has never been measured
issues.found_on: every figure here stops at golive's edge
issues.symptom: The gateway, the PBX and the phone network, both ways, are on top of every number in this journal. On the first recorded call, echoprobe found no echo of the assistant's voice at any delay up to 1.5 s (significance 1.9 against a threshold of 6.0): a quiet handset cancels its own echo.
issues.cause: Nothing outside golive reports a timestamp; the owner's console holds only golive's own events.
issues.fix: Not fixed. What is left is a recording made beside the handset during a call, lined up with the box's recording of the same call.

issues.title: Recognition on phone audio is poor
issues.found_on: several calls: wrong words
issues.symptom: Words are misrecognized on the phone line.
issues.cause: The 16 kHz engine is run on audio the phone network has band-limited to 8 kHz.
issues.fix: Untried: the 8k_zh engine, which needs the adapter to send 8 kHz audio.

issues.title: A phone line is never quiet, and returns the assistant's voice
issues.found_on: second real call
issues.symptom: A finished question was held open for 3.3 s on line noise; an answer was thrown away eight times. On out-mv4rvtp9-d3fw one of two interruptions was flagged as possibly the assistant's own voice returning.
issues.cause: The energy detector never saw silence; the assistant's own voice came back loud enough to read as the caller.
issues.fix: settled_close_ms, vad.echo_tail_ms, vad.barge_in_margin_db.
issues.verified: One 'looks like the assistant's own voice' warning per call remains.

issues.title: Outbound calls ended in 408 with the phone never ringing
issues.found_on: several attempts to place a call
issues.symptom: Every outbound call timed out after 32 s.
issues.cause: The GSM gateway changes its SIP port when it re-registers; the PBX trunk pointed at the old one.
issues.fix: A timer on the box keeps the trunk in step with the gateway (outside this repository).

issues.title: Any word the caller murmured stopped the assistant, and a listed murmur lost its head start
issues.found_on: the owner's review of the backchannel settings
issues.symptom: The phone profile's list of murmurs was empty, so "嗯" or "对" said over an answer cut it off. And any word put on the list would have had its turns answered without a head start when said into a silence.
issues.cause: The list was shipped empty on purpose (each entry is a phrase the caller can no longer interrupt with). The list was also consulted when deciding whether to begin an answer early, wherever the word was said.
issues.fix: The owner's 33 phrases are in the phone profile. The list now only decides who has the floor: a listed word said while the assistant is silent is begun on its early final like any short turn.
issues.effect: A listed word said into a silence came up three times and was answered each time with its head start. No murmur was said over the assistant on that call, so keeping the floor through one is still not heard on a line; seven real interruptions were each recognised 0.1 to 0.4 s in.
issues.note: 10-13 21:15 call: a listed murmur said twelve times, each into a silence and each answered with its head start; none said over the assistant, so the keeping of the floor is still not seen on a call.

issues.title: A call's recording was deleted after a week, and its text lived in one log file
issues.found_on: the owner asking for persistent storage of every call
issues.symptom: Recordings expired after 7 days. The conversation and the measurements existed only as the journal's reading of a single log file.
issues.cause: golive's store is working storage with a retention; nothing was built to keep a call.
issues.fix: An archive on the box that nothing deletes from: per call, the recording as one stereo file, the conversation to read, everything measured, golive's own session record and the call's lines of the log, with checksums. The journal feeds it between calls and plays from it. A second copy on another disk is one command, not yet scheduled.
issues.effect: The call was archived, recording and text, within a minute of ending, with nobody opening the page.

issues.title: The pool treated a ten-a-minute account like a thirty-a-minute one
issues.found_on: pacing the second account alone after its first call
issues.symptom: Nothing was lost on the call. Paced alone at 30 requests a minute, the second account refused 42 of 76 requests from the 28th second on; the first has carried 22 to 31 a minute unrefused. With one limit for both, a busy call that found both counted full stayed on whichever account it was on, including the small one past its real limit, and a refused request had nowhere to go when the other account was counted full.
issues.cause: One `tts_account_rpm` for every account, taken from the vendor's page; and the rule for a full account only moved a session to an account with room left, never to the roomier of two full ones.
issues.fix: Each account's allowance is written beside its key (`MINIMAX_TTS_RPM=20`, `MINIMAX_TTS_RPM_2=8`: the vendor's page gives a topped-up account 20 a minute and a free one 10) and counted by itself; with both full the session goes to the roomier account; a request an account refuses is asked of the other at once, room or no room, and the refusing account is treated as full for the minute.
issues.effect: All 13 turns were asked of both accounts; the second spoke first 7 times, the first 6; nothing refused and neither account reached its limit.
issues.note: 10-13 21:15 call, 47 turns: 33 first segments asked of both accounts (17 and 13 first), four moves between accounts, about 21 requests a minute, nothing refused.

issues.title: The caller's side of a recording ran late against the assistant's
issues.found_on: the owner reading the 21:15 call's conversation against its recording
issues.symptom: In the journal a caller's question was stamped at 1:40 and its answer at 1:41, but in the recording the question was heard about two seconds later, after the answer had begun; by the end of the call the caller's side was six seconds late. The stamps and every latency figure were right: they come from the log's clock, and the assistant's side of the recording matched them within 0.16 s all call long.
issues.cause: The phone side delivered the caller's audio faster than time passed: a 20 ms chunk every 19.6 ms on this call. Nine evening calls show it (19.4 to 19.6 ms a chunk), four daytime calls do not (19.97 to 20.02). The recorder appended the caller's audio as it arrived and only ever corrected a track that had fallen behind the clock, never one that had run ahead. Why the phone side does it is not known.
issues.fix: The recorder leaves out a chunk that is the previous chunk over again, the frame a quiet line repeats, while the caller's track is ahead of the clock; speech is never dropped. For recordings made before that, the journal does the same as it plays them, from the log's marks of how much audio had arrived by when, says how much it left out, and offers the file exactly as recorded. A caller's line is now stamped where it began, as the assistant's are.
issues.note: Checked on the 21:15 call as the journal now plays it: 6.2 s of repeated quiet frames left out, and the caller's words end within 0.15 to 0.25 s of their stamps in the first, middle and last third alike (as recorded they slid by seconds). The recorder's own correction is in build b5ad7c6 and recorded its first call at 15:37 on 10-14: the session record says the caller's track was kept on the clock, and the journal applied no correction. Open: what upstream sends 2% more audio than time on evening calls (gateway, PBX or phone bridge).

issues.title: A murmur said as the answer ended was answered as a turn
issues.found_on: the 15:44 call, 3657 ms turn
issues.symptom: The caller said a listed murmur over the last word of an answer. The floor was kept and the answer not interrupted, but an answer to the murmur was begun, held, and spoken 2.7 s later, and the turn counted at 3657 ms.
issues.cause: Whether words are an acknowledgement was judged by whether the assistant was speaking at that instant. The murmur's words arrived a moment after the audio ended, while the floor hold opened during the audio was still pending, so the words read as a turn; and a hold's verdict swallowed the utterance without abandoning the guess already begun on it.
issues.fix: A pending floor hold counts as the assistant having the floor; a swallowed utterance abandons any speculation begun on it.
issues.note: To be seen on the next call with a murmur over the assistant.

issues.title: Speaker-focus labels fall behind on long utterances
issues.found_on: the 19:34 call, item_6
issues.symptom: On a 2.2 s utterance the diarizer's labels arrived 1,660 ms behind the audio, after the answer's first audio (heard=true); on the shorter utterance of the same call 480 ms, on the 13:52 call 360 ms. In veto mode a background voice that long could not be vetoed before it was answered.
issues.cause: The model server runs at about real time on the ThinkPad's CPU (~330 ms per 345 ms chunk at steady state) and queues chunks during a long stretch of speech instead of catching up.
issues.fix: edge/diar_server.py --max-backlog (1): chunks queued beyond it are skipped unlabelled so the labels stay within about one chunk of the audio; the skipped span gets no frames, so the client's coverage says it is missing. Unverified on a call.

issues.title: A noisy line kept an utterance open for 30 s: the energy gate and the recognizer both called the noise speech
issues.found_on: the 19:41 call, first 40 s
issues.symptom: After the caller's first words the detector stayed active for 29 of 30 s (no 380 quiet ms on the line) and the recognizer produced a new hypothesis every 0.5–1 s from the background sound, so the settled close never saw unchanged words. The utterance ended at the 30 s cap; the assistant was silent for ~35 s.
issues.cause: Both end-of-turn witnesses are fooled by the same noise: the energy gate by its level, the recognizer by transcribing it. The diarizer on the focus side channel labelled only 2,160 ms of voice in those 29 s but is not consulted for ending turns, and its labels were 3.4 s behind by then (ISS-032).
issues.fix: vad.floor_track_ms (2000): the quietest frame of the last 2 s of an open utterance becomes the floor when nothing in that time dipped under the bar, so the noise stops reading as voiced and the utterance closes on the caller's next 380 quiet ms. Test: a steady rumble closes within 3.5 s, a 4 s sentence is heard to its end. The gate's record is kept in session.json and drawn in the journal (the Gate lane).

issues.title: A background voice, or the assistant's own echo, cut the answer: the hold trusted the recognizer's words
issues.found_on: the 21:59 call, 30 answers cut
issues.symptom: With an English-language show in the caller's background the answer was cut 30 times in 3.7 minutes: 20 utterances opened over the assistant's speech at exactly 320 ms, the recognizer made words of the show (or of the assistant's echo at −28 dB), and the hold ruled them not a backchannel.
issues.cause: The floor hold had one witness, the recognizer, and the recognizer transcribes any voice. The speaker labels knew (two of the judged utterances had no voice at all, one was entirely another voice's, labels 280–520 ms behind) but were not asked about barge-ins, and the tracker masked everything said while the assistant spoke.
issues.fix: Tracker.Echo tells the assistant's return apart (the voice heard mostly while the assistant speaks, ≥800 ms, ≥70% of its activity); Tracker.AttributeOver reads a span through the masks with the echo taken out; judgeBargeInFocus holds a barge-in with words for the labels up to focus_barge_in_wait_ms (900): the caller's voice (≥160 ms) yields, another voice or the echo alone keeps the floor and the utterance goes by without a turn unless the caller joins in; in observe mode the verdict is logged and the words decide. The telephony profile goes to focus: veto. Tests: TestASoundOverTheAnswerIsReadWithTheEchoTakenOut, TestAnotherVoiceOverTheAnswerDoesNotCutIt.
issues.verified_on: out-mv9mxpzt-0ur9 (22:29): the path fired once in time (one answer kept) and 37 times too late — the diarizer's labels 1–1.2 s behind under continuous background speech. Superseded by ISS-035.

issues.title: The diarizer's labels fall seconds behind under continuous background speech, so every judgment on them comes too late
issues.found_on: the 22:29 call, 38 barge-ins judged, 1 in time
issues.symptom: With a show in the background the diarizer's labels were 340–480 ms behind at the start of the call and 1–1.2 s behind within a minute; 37 of 38 sounds over the answer were decided on the recognizer's words because the labels had not arrived inside the 900 ms wait; two of the show's lines were answered before the labels came.
issues.cause: Nemotron-3-Diarization runs at about real time on the ThinkPad's CPU; continuous speech leaves it no gap to catch up, and skipping chunks does not hold it under a second.
issues.fix: A target-speaker service (edge/tsv_server.py, CAM++ zh/en embedding, 10 ms a window) in place of the diarizer on the focus channel: the caller's voice is enrolled from their first utterance alone (extended by the next few the labels call theirs), every 100 ms window is scored against it, labels one window behind. The engine judges the open utterance as it is said (judgeUtteranceFocus): not the caller's and it goes by with no turn. Tests: TestABackgroundVoicesUtteranceIsLetGoBy; measured on the archive: caller 0.45–0.68, assistant 0.14–0.21, the show under 0.25 against a 2 s enrolment.
issues.verified_on: out-mv9oqusr-3h0z (23:20): labels 0–140 ms behind, every judgment in time; but four of the caller's own utterances were vetoed as another voice's — under the show every window is a mixture and scores 0.1–0.4. Retuned: a verdict needs zero primary voice; enrolment from the first utterance only; threshold 0.28. See ISS-036.

issues.title: With a show under the caller's voice, speaker verification cannot separate them: the caller's own answers were vetoed
issues.found_on: the 23:20 call, 4 of the caller's answers dropped unheard
issues.symptom: Four of the caller's utterances were judged another voice's and their answers dropped; the caller's windows scored 0.1–0.4 against the enrolment (quiet line: 0.42–0.63), because every 800 ms window was a mixture of the caller and the show.
issues.cause: A speaker-embedding score on overlapped speech is the score of the mixture; a 70% 'other' share is routine for the caller talking over a television. Extending the enrolment with such utterances put the show into the enrolment.
issues.fix: Mitigation: every verdict requires zero primary voice (a mixture is the caller), focus_veto_share 0.95, enrolment from the first utterance only, threshold 0.28. Real fix, to evaluate: target-speaker extraction (removing everything but the enrolled voice from the audio before the gate and the recognizer), if a model runs in real time on the box's CPU.

issues.title: A guess was kept though two more characters followed it: any number of trailing sounds counted as none
issues.found_on: the 09:16 call, two turns
issues.symptom: An answer begun on the words before a 200 ms pause was kept while two more characters arrived, and answered a shorter question than was asked.
issues.cause: sameWords read any run of trailing particles (啊呀哦…) as the caller finishing, so two real characters that happened to be in the set passed.
issues.fix: One trailing sound, not more; a second character is words and the guess is remade.

issues.title: The channel enrolled 'not the caller' as the primary and inverted every verdict; a one-utterance enrolment does not represent a voice on a phone line
issues.found_on: the 09:41 call, primary_speaker=1
issues.symptom: Three of the owner's answers vetoed as another voice's, three utterances let go by, five answers cut, on a call that was the owner's voice alone.
issues.cause: The enrolment taken from the first utterance scored the owner's own later utterances at 0.07–0.25, so the service labelled them 'not the caller'; the tracker's first-voice rule then enrolled that label as the primary and every verdict came out inverted.
issues.fix: The caller is whoever picked up, learned from the call: up to six caller-alone utterances are offered and the enrolment is the largest mutually agreeing group (one alone tentative, outvotable; later ones join only if they agree). The caller is pinned as the primary on the channel; an enrolment the next 8 s contradict is distrusted and the channel observes only. focus_profile (a kept embedding) is optional, for a line that always reaches one person; empty on the test line.

issues.title: A bad one-window enrolment inverted the focus labels: the caller became 'another voice' and three answers were vetoed
issues.found_on: the 09:41 call, caller alone
issues.symptom: On a quiet call with the caller alone, 3 answers vetoed as another voice's, 3 utterances let go by; primary_speaker=1.
issues.cause: The 1.3 s enrolment window was a poor sample (the caller's later utterances 0.07–0.25 against it, 0.54–0.59 against the previous call's), and the tracker's own enrolment rule then took the 'not the caller' label as the primary.
issues.fix: The caller is whoever picked up, learned from the call: up to six caller-alone utterances are offered and the enrolment is the largest mutually agreeing group (one alone tentative, outvotable; later ones join only if they agree). The caller is pinned as the primary on the channel; an enrolment the next 8 s contradict is distrusted and the channel observes only. focus_profile (a kept embedding) is optional, for a line that always reaches one person; empty on the test line.

issues.title: The simulated customer's gateway ends every call at about 145 s
issues.found_on: the first two multi-turn simulated calls
issues.symptom: Both conversations ended at 144.15 s and 145.05 s, mid-utterance, with the receiver reporting 'Active Call control disconnected' and RustPBX 'Callee initiated hangup (UasBye)' from 172.20.0.2: the BYE came from the simulator's gateway. No scenario limit was near (290 s, 40 turns, 20 s idle).
issues.cause: The receiver counts a remote turn per speech burst (each synthesized segment after a pause), so max_remote_turns is reached at roughly half the answers: 40 → 135–145 s, 80 → 200 s. A limit stop was reported as 'Active Call control disconnected' until Codex's ae89b93 added termination attribution (local_reason 'remote turn limit'). The 09:38–10:04 endings at 80–82 s were a second cause, a synthesizer error ending the call, fixed in ae89b93.
issues.fix: Scenarios at the cap (max_remote_turns 100) so the 295 s duration binds; Codex asked (desk n21) to count per debounced utterance and to end a limit stop as completed.
issues.verified_on: out-mvbsnh36-xtgf: 200 s, 42 turns, attribution 'remote turn limit'

issues.title: A SIP peer with silence suppression starved both recognizers: one-turn conversations
issues.found_on: the first simulated calls on real providers
issues.symptom: Every call: one greeting each way, then nothing; Tencent gave up after 15 s of no audio on both sides (the customer's at exactly 8.62 + 15.0 s, 'voice engine failed').
issues.cause: Neither gateway sends RTP while nobody speaks (a GSM line sends a frame every 20 ms). The gate and the recognizer count pauses in the audio that arrives, so the pause that closes an utterance never arrived.
issues.fix: vad.line_fill_ms (100): when no client frame has come for that long, 20 ms of silence is pushed per 20 ms on the wall clock until audio returns; the recording gets the same. The receiver got the same from Codex (a4f77d5).
issues.verified_on: out-mvb3zqbe-4e4l: 144 s, 30 assistant / 61 customer utterances, 96.9 s filled

issues.title: After end_call the model was resumed with the tool's output and said goodbye a second time, cut off by the hangup
issues.found_on: the first call on which the assistant hung up (simulated)
issues.symptom: The farewell played in full (1126 ms), the engine resumed the backend with end_call's result as with any tool, the model answered with a second farewell (6 characters, from the phrase cache) which began 391 ms before the hangup and was cut after ~400 ms. The quiet check had passed before it started; the grace did not look again.
issues.cause: continueWith() after server-side tool calls did not know the conversation was over; endCallWhenQuiet() slept the grace once and hung up without re-checking the player.
issues.fix: An accepted end_call ends the response: the backend is not resumed with its output (hangingUp()). endCallWhenQuiet re-checks the player after the grace and waits again if something began to play. Test: TestTheAssistantHangsUpAfterItsFarewellHasPlayed, whose scripted model now says goodbye again when resumed.

issues.title: The simulated customer reports the assistant's hangup as a failure and keeps no response gaps
issues.found_on: out-mvc8lypr-bnxc
issues.symptom: golive hung up after the farewell (BYE from Active Call); the run ended `failed: Active Call control disconnected`, 20 s later, after an 'inactivity limit' stop; checks indeterminate, 0 valid assistant_response_gaps, no completed report. Also: a run reserved on the desk at midday had expired to `failed` by 18:10 and the first dial went to it.
issues.cause: The receiver treats the far end's BYE as its control link dropping rather than as the call ending; the desk does not show a reservation's expiry.
issues.fix: Asked of Codex (desk n23): a remote BYE ends the run `completed` with termination_reason `remote_hangup` and the full report. On our side: `call sim` should check the reserved run's phase before dialling and reserve afresh if it is not waiting.

issues.title: Background noise kept the caller's turn open: the floor and the settled close both need the line, and the recognizer kept finding words in the noise
issues.found_on: a real call, noisy room (the owner said so)
issues.symptom: One utterance open 9 s (55.5–64.5 s), 6.3 s judged voiced, labels: primary 0.5 / others 0.5 over 8.2 s; the recognizer's hypothesis grew 13→14→20 chars of repeated words, two speculative turns abandoned as it moved on, the turn taken by the 900 ms patience; 1525 ms from the caller's last sound for an answer the engine made in 625. Three further turns ended by the settled close after 600 ms (1065–1101 from last sound).
issues.cause: The detector's pause needs the line quiet; the floor tracker needs the noise steady and under the voice; the settled close needs the recognizer's words to stand still, and on noise it keeps producing new ones. None of the three asks whose voice is on the line.
issues.fix: duplex.focus_quiet_close_ms (420, telephony): the turn is taken when the focus labels show the caller's voice absent for that long while the gate stays open, once the utterance is theirs; counted as quiet_closes. Test: TestTheTurnIsTakenWhenTheCallerGoesQuietThoughTheLineDoesNot (fails with it off).
issues.verified_on: out-mvfzqdsc-fz8a (metro station): 11 quiet closes, no misfire; see also out-mveluuk3-n4bu

issues.title: A caller who answers fast and interrupts is never enrolled, and the focus channel then does nothing for the whole call
issues.found_on: a real call from a metro station
issues.symptom: judged=0, primary_speaker=-1 at the end of a 63 s call; all four sounds over the answer judged 'no primary speaker known yet' and yielded on words; a station announcement cut a 3.9 s answer and was answered.
issues.cause: enrolFocus offered only utterances clean from their first millisecond: not a barge-in, not within the 600 ms echo tail of the assistant's last word, 600 ms voiced. The caller replied within 0.9 s of the greeting and interrupted four of six answers; nothing qualified.
issues.fix: The clean tail is offered: from Tracker.MaskedUntil(start, end+tail) to the utterance's end when the proportional voiced part is >= 600 ms; barge-ins included. Logged with trimmed_ms and barge_in.
issues.verified_on: out-mvfzqdsc-fz8a: enrolled 18 s in from the first utterance, 6/6 agreeing; five other voices let go by, one barge-in kept

issues.title: The assistant's hangup closed golive's socket but the phone line stayed up
issues.found_on: the first real call that ended with a goodbye
issues.symptom: end_call accepted, farewell played, session closed assistant_hangup at 23:16:33; the owner heard the goodbye and the line stayed up until he hung up (his word: option 1).
issues.cause: Active Call hangs up on a command from its controller (Aria) over the control WebSocket or POST /command/<dialog>; the agent's socket closing is not that.
issues.fix: config.HangupURL (telephony: http://127.0.0.1:8081/command/{call}); Session.hangupLine POSTs the hangup command there before closing. The route and body are what Codex's receiver uses (his reply over Reason Network, 08:51).
issues.verified_on: out-mvfzqdsc-fz8a: the gateway was told to hang up status=200; the line dropped

issues.title: The farewell was cut by a sound over it and the line dropped mid-word
issues.found_on: a real call from a metro station; the owner heard it
issues.symptom: end_call accepted with an 11-character farewell; at 770 ms a sound over it was taken as a barge-in, the farewell truncated at 4 characters, a new turn begun on the sound; hangup 700 ms later. The caller heard four characters and the click.
issues.cause: After end_call the engine still treated the farewell as any answer: yieldFloor cut it on a barge-in, beginGeneration answered the sound.
issues.fix: While hangingUp(): yieldFloor keeps the floor, beginGeneration starts nothing, Interrupt is ignored; endCallWhenQuiet then waits for the whole farewell. Test: TestTheFarewellIsNotCutByASoundOverIt.

issues.title: The model said goodbye twice without calling end_call; the line stayed up
issues.found_on: a real call; the owner: 'the hangup was postponed'
issues.symptom: item_13 and item_14 (3 and 6 characters, 再见) with tool_calls=0; no end_call on the call; the caller spoke twice more and hung up at 10:01:03.
issues.cause: The hangup depended on the model remembering the tool in the same breath as its farewell; it does not always.
issues.fix: An 'assistant' hangup rule, judged by the engine on the reply it has just finished saying (checkAssistantHangupRules, on turn completion): a match ends the call by the end_call path. In the default set as said_goodbye (再见|拜拜|不打扰您了); added to the box's hangup-rules as v2. Test: TestAGoodbyeSaidWithoutTheToolStillEndsTheCall.
